notices.short_title: OPEN-ENDED  JUSTICE INVOLVED SUPPORTIVE HOUSING (JISH) RFP
notices.description:
The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene ('Health Department') continues to seek proposals for the Justice Involved Supportive Housing (Open-Ended) Request for Proposals (RFP) through the City's Procurement and Sourcing Solutions Portal ('PASSPort' system).

This RFP is intended to procure and make available permanent supportive housing units for adults (18+); initially, the Health Department anticipates that the population would be comprised mainly of individuals who are frequently cycling through jail and shelter who have a mental illness and/or substance use disorder. The Health Department anticipates that the population matches may expand to include individuals who, in addition to having frequent contact with the criminal justice system and the homeless system, have also had frequent contact with the mental health treatment system.

RFP documents and additional details can be found by visiting the PASSPort Pr…
notices.plain: The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene is seeking proposals through an open-ended request for proposals for permanent supportive housing units for adults, mainly people who repeatedly cycle through jail and shelters and have a mental illness or substance use disorder, with responses due Dec. 31, 2026.

notices.description:
DHS/HSO intends to enter into a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) for on-site medical and behavioral services at Atlantic Assessment Mens Shelter with current provider Sunset Park Health Council Inc. DBA Family Health Centers at NYU Langone. Medical and Behavioral Health Services at the Atlantic Assessment Men's Shelter @ 1322 Bedford Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11216.

The proposed budget for this NAE is $1,670,545.00 and the term of this extension is from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027. The Health Service Office is currently drafting a new RFP.
Procurement and award are in accordance with PPB Rules Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) for the reasons set forth herein.
notices.plain: The Department of Homeless Services awarded Sunset Park Health Council Inc. a $2.2 million negotiated extension for on-site medical and behavioral health services at Atlantic Assessment Men's Shelter, Oct. 1, 2026, to Sept. 30, 2027.

notices.description: NYC Parks would like to partner with an outside vendor that specializes in a Cyber Security Assessment process and in building security strategies. This strategy will align with OTIs Cyber Command and industry best practices. This assessment will be able to provide NYC Parks direction on our current security vulnerabilities; build a roadmap for improving our overall security posture and strengthen our alignment for the city; and identify and validate weaknesses in the NYC Parks information security architecture and posture from both an internal and external vantage point.
notices.plain: The Department of Parks and Recreation awarded Svam International Inc a $265,000 contract, without open competition, for a cyber security audit that will assess the agency's security weaknesses and recommend a plan to improve them.

notices.description: Cornerstone Community Centers provide engaging activities year-round for young people and adults. Programs are located at 99 New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) Community Centers throughout the five boroughs, and were shaped by input from young people, NYCHA residents, Resident Association leaders, elected officials, and principals at schools that serve youth who live in the participating developments.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded BronxWorks Inc a $11.7 million negotiated contract, announced Nov. 6, 2026, to run Cornerstone Community Centers, which offer year-round activities for young people and adults at 99 New York City Housing Authority community centers across the five boroughs.

notices.description: COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. Programs are offered at no cost to youth and are purposefully located in public and private schools, community centers, religious institutions, public housing and parks recreational facilities throughout the City to help families find a place that best fits their youth's needs. Center Based services for elementary in Brooklyn 08 located at 1181 E New York Avenue, Zip code 11212.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Inner Force Economic Development Corp a $3,488,400 contract, chosen from competing proposals and a pre-qualified list, to run COMPASS center-based after-school and summer programs for elementary students at 1181 E New York Avenue in Brooklyn.
